source.title: Understanding activation patterns in artificial neural networks by exploring stochastic processes: Discriminating generalization from memorization
source.authors: S. Lehmler; Muhammad Saif-ur-Rehman; T. Glasmachers; Ioannis Iossifidis

record.file_problem: The supplied text is the full paper; no material document problem noted.
record.tranche_reason: It trains networks on randomized labels and reports their training and validation accuracies, but uses this as a setup for activation-pattern analysis rather than reproducing the original study’s full evaluation.
record.gate_note: Table 1 reports accuracies for generalization and three randomized-label memorization settings. The randomized-label results bear on V1. The paper does not test optimization time, unstructured inputs, graded label noise, regularization, or learning order.
record.test_reason: Table 1 measures randomized-label training accuracy and held-out validation accuracy using SGD, directly testing V1 with the same basic method and measures as the original. The activation analysis is the main purpose, but the paper also reports its own memorization results.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is broadly accurate if memorization includes partial fitting. The authors find varied randomized-label fitting and propose activation statistics as indicators distinguishing generalization from memorization. They report lower mean firing rates during memorization, attenuation of this difference when earlier layers can memorize, and stabilization after the imposed label switch. They acknowledge limitations of the Poisson fit and the need for broader validation.
record.recipe_differences: The paper uses a randomized-label memorization setup on MNIST, FashionMNIST and CIFAR-10, with SGD (learning rate 0.1, batch size 256, momentum disabled). It varies initialization and which layers are trainable; models and hyperparameters were selected by grid search for both generalization and memorization.
record.method_sensitivity: Training accuracy depends strongly on dataset, width, architecture, initialization and whether layers before the last two are trainable.

fits_no_version.finding: Memorizing models generally have lower mean firing rates and higher mean Fano factors; differences depend on observed-layer width and which earlier layers can train.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Thresholded activation statistics can distinguish separately trained generalizing and memorizing networks in some settings.

fits_no_version.finding: Mean firing rate changes and then stabilizes after an experimentally imposed switch from correct to randomized labels.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Activation statistics respond to a change in training-label regime; this does not establish real-label-first learning within noisy data.

record.problems: The study grid-searched model and hyperparameter choices to enable both generalization and memorization; some reported configurations memorize only part of the randomized training set. Training accuracy values are from the flattened Table 1, with no uncertainty estimates stated.
record.rows_left_out: None. Kept 60 rows, the maximum allowed; no additional Table 1 randomized-label accuracy results omitted.

untested.parts: Unrestricted training from random initialization for CNN and DenseNet; independent confirmation outside the jointly selected models and hyperparameters; matched stopping rules and training budgets. The paper does explicitly report shared architectures and SGD hyperparameters across label conditions.

Time or updates needed to reach comparable training error, the constant-factor comparison, and convergence as label corruption increases. The scheduled 10 clean-label epochs followed by 100 random-label epochs do not establish these.
Fitting shuffled-pixel, independently permuted-pixel, or Gaussian-noise inputs. The reported shuffling concerns label randomization, not these input transformations.
Intermediate corruption fractions, perfect fitting throughout a noise sweep, and steady degradation of test performance toward chance.
Effects of adding or removing weight decay, dropout, and data augmentation on random-label fitting and true-label generalization.
Whether shared real-data patterns are learned before noisy labels under a common training condition. Clean-label training followed by an imposed label switch does not test spontaneous learning order.

record.verdict_notes: Table 1 has 52 distinct randomized-label accuracy results, not 60: eight MLP MemRetrainAll entries were invented by extending a column that begins at the CNN block. Several MemRandomLast values were also copied from adjacent columns. Verdicts use corrected associations. Held-out values are validation accuracies from a 10% validation split, not independently reported test accuracies. Joint grid search selected models capable of both tasks; the paper explicitly states that optimizer and training hyperparameters were shared. Frozen-layer failures qualify those restricted settings and do not establish failure of unrestricted network training.

versions.untested_parts: Tests randomized labels on MNIST, FashionMNIST and CIFAR-10 with selected architectures; does not establish the broader claim across standard deep networks or compare every setting to unchanged original hyperparameters.
